open_points.subject: M11 owner-session time facts
open_points.text: State 1 says "Every time Registry records is an instant in UTC with time zone" and describes M11 facts as "the instant it began", "the instant of its last request" and "the instant it was shown"; changed A13 says those facts "are held as readings of that monotonic clock" and that "the UTC rule for recorded times does not reach them".
open_points.question: Are M11's temporal facts UTC instants as State 1 specifies, or monotonic-clock readings as changed A13 specifies?
options: Keep them solely as monotonic readings and amend M11 and the general State 1 time rule
Keep UTC instants as M11 facts and derive limits from separate monotonic readings
Treat in-memory session facts as outside the meaning of "Registry records"
open_points.default_guess: Treat the changed A13 as controlling: store only monotonic readings for M11 and amend State 1 accordingly.

open_points.subject: owner-session clock capability
open_points.text: The session clock is required to be a "monotonic clock ... which counts the time the host or its VM was suspended", but no required clock source, capability check or failure rule is stated.
open_points.question: How must Registry establish that its clock counts both host and VM suspension, and what happens at start if the runtime or hypervisor cannot provide that guarantee?
options: Require a named suspend-aware clock and fail startup when unavailable
Make a suspend-aware clock a deployment prerequisite that Registry does not verify
Permit a fallback clock even though sessions may outlive suspension
open_points.default_guess: Require a suspend-aware boot-time clock and fail startup if it is unavailable.

open_points.subject: 60-second owner-session expiry pass
open_points.text: Registry makes a pass "every 60 seconds from the start", but the text does not say what happens when a pass lasts longer than 60 seconds or when suspension causes several scheduled instants to pass.
open_points.question: Are passes fixed-rate or fixed-delay, may they overlap, and after missed intervals does Registry run one pass immediately, run several catch-up passes, or wait for the next interval?
options: Non-overlapping fixed-rate passes, coalescing missed intervals into one immediate pass
Non-overlapping passes scheduled 60 seconds after the preceding pass finishes
Overlapping fixed-rate passes for every elapsed interval
open_points.default_guess: Use non-overlapping fixed-rate passes and coalesce all missed intervals into one immediate pass.

open_points.subject: backup encryption construction
open_points.text: A18 says each backup "is encrypted with the backup key" and records "a digest of the key", but declares no encryption or authentication algorithm, nonce rule, key interpretation or digest algorithm.
open_points.question: What exact authenticated-encryption construction and key-digest construction must every release use, including nonce generation, key encoding or derivation, algorithm/version identification and failure handling?
options: Declare one versioned authenticated-encryption file format using the configured secret as a raw key
Declare a password-based KDF followed by a versioned authenticated-encryption format
Allow each release to choose its own construction and record the choice in the backup
open_points.default_guess: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption format with random nonces, a fixed cryptographic key digest and the configured secret treated as raw key material.

open_points.subject: unencrypted backup record
open_points.text: The backup's instant, release, last sequence number and key digest are "readable without its key"; the text does not say whether that unencrypted record is cryptographically authenticated with the encrypted store.
open_points.question: Can the unencrypted record be altered independently, or must authentication bind it to the encrypted payload so that altered metadata is unreadable or invalid for listing, retention and restore checks?
options: Authenticate the entire record as associated data of the encrypted payload
Sign or MAC the record separately with the backup key
Leave the record unauthenticated and trust filesystem administration
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate the complete unencrypted record as associated data of the encrypted payload.

open_points.subject: valid kept-backup record
open_points.text: A kept file's record is valid when its "instant, release, last sequence number and key digest can all be read"; no semantic validity rules are given for those values.
open_points.question: Which parseable but nonsensical values make the record invalid—for example a future or non-UTC instant, a negative sequence number, an unknown release, a digest of the wrong algorithm or length, or metadata inconsistent with the kept filename?
options: Specify strict types, ranges, supported algorithms and filename consistency
Treat any syntactically decodable values as valid
Validate only the instant and sequence number, treating release and digest as opaque text
open_points.default_guess: Specify strict types and ranges, a supported metadata version and algorithms, and consistency between the record and kept filename.

open_points.subject: store and backup-location encryption at rest
open_points.text: "The store, the backup location and the disks under them are encrypted and kept out of VM Agent's reach by the owner's administration" while "Registry does not check the host."
open_points.question: What concrete host controls satisfy this requirement, and what evidence or verification closes it if Registry performs no check?
options: Require specified full-disk or volume encryption and VM isolation, verified by deployment tests
Treat encryption and VM isolation as an unverified owner assertion
Require application-level store encryption in addition to encrypted backups
open_points.default_guess: Require documented volume encryption and VM isolation with deployment-level verification outside Registry.
